analysis:
The PR only modifies docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 2336-2348): one added paragraph describing constrained-decode chaining for FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint, mask caching keyed by constraint state, and RecursiveSI/flint-int4 on the automatic paged list at the legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. The supplied units (base lines 802-1635) are unchanged context and contain none of the changed lines. No code, configuration, or policy change is in this batch, so no security control is altered.

Threat-model relevance, all informational only: the paragraph describes behavior in the CBv2 engine (constrained chaining, per-row RNG and penalty state restoration) and the serving-width list. These touch TB-007 (inference engine) and T-029/T-010-style availability concerns. The document asserts the token stream is identical to unchained decode. That is an unverified claim, since the implementing code is not supplied. Cached device masks keyed by constraint state also raise a theoretical question: whether mask reuse could cross request or tenant scope. The mask depends only on the constraint state, not on prompt data, so no tenant data or A-001 exposure is evident.

T-041 (prefix cache and TTFT oracle) is unaffected, because media and constrained paths do not change cache scoping or SSD tier behavior in the supplied text. Remaining integration questions for any code-bearing pass: the actual chaining and redraw implementation must restore RNG, penalty and logit state exactly, or output could diverge. The width increase for flint-int4 should stay bounded by the memory admission and KV budget checks. Neither can be verified from documentation alone, and neither is a finding here.
